subject: Presidio: Renewal uplift, performance arbitration, and bridge offer
messages:
From: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@presidio.ai>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: laura.chen@presidio.ai, procurement@presidio.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Upcoming renewal & perf questions

Vivek —

Quick note as we dig into our renewal later this quarter. We ran an internal perf comparison last week between Redwood and a competing provider. Two things that matter to us: 1) tail latency on 2k token requests during peak, and 2) predictable throughput when we push concurrent batches at end of day. The competing provider shows a consistent 12–18% latency advantage in those scenarios.

Before we push the RFP further, can Redwood share any recent benchmark results or a short proposal that addresses the gap? If we can get a clear path to matching latency and an option to pilot a capacity uplift for Q3, that would keep us from switching vendors mid-year.

Attaching the internal summary for context. Happy to set a quick call this week.

Regards,
Tom
VP Engineering, Presidio AI

Attachment: presidio_internal_summary.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
To: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@presidio.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2029 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal & perf questions

Tom —

Thanks for flagging this and for the summary. Short answer: we can close most of that gap operationally without moving away from your current model version. I want to propose two things:

1) A focused benchmark run (we'll run on your production-like prompt set) within 72 hours and share an apples-to-apples PDF.
2) A 90-day uplift pilot for +25% reserved capacity with an SLA-backed latency window and a one-time bridge credit on unit price if we miss agreed targets.

I'll kick this to Marissa to own the benchmark and to Ben for commercial shape. Can you send the canonical prompt set (or a redacted subset) and confirm peak windows (PST hours)?

Call options: Wed 10–11am or Thu 2–3pm PT.

Best,
Vivek
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

---
vivek_kulkarni
Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@presidio.ai>, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2029 08:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal & perf questions

Tom —

We're scheduled to run the benchmark tomorrow with a config that mirrors your reported load: concurrent batches = 28, sequence length tail = 2k, sampling seeds aligned to your prompts. I'll attach the run artifact and an initial PDF with latency percentiles and confidence intervals.

Preliminary note: in our previous bench we saw variance driven by two factors — KV cache hit rate and batch packing inefficiency at high concurrency. For the pilot we recommend enabling prefix caching and conservative packing thresholds; that usually yields a consistent 10–15% tail-latency improvement.

Attaching: presidio_bench_report_v2.pdf (results)

Next actions from our side:
- Deliver final bench PDF by EOD Thu
- Draft term sheet for 90-day uplift pilot (+25% capacity) by Fri morning
- Proposal will include a one-time bridge credit (covers 30% of uplift cost) and an SLA clause for p95 latency during peak windows

If that lines up, Ben and I will join the Thu call to walk through results and commercial terms.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachment: presidio_bench_report_v2.pdf

From: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@presidio.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: laura.chen@presidio.ai, procurement@presidio.ai
Date: Thu, 4 Apr 2029 10:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal & perf questions

Marissa / Vivek —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the PDF — we reviewed it with engineering. The numbers look closer, and the caching suggestions make sense. Two outstanding concerns from our infra team:

1) How disruptive is enabling prefix caching to our runtime (do we need app changes)?
2) The competitor's offer includes an operational runway guarantee (free burst for seasonal peaks for the first month). Can Redwood match a similar temporary burst guarantee during our busiest week?

We can join Thu 2pm. I'll come with a list of follow-ups the infra team wants answered live.

Tom

---
Presidio AI

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@presidio.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 4 Apr 2029 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal & perf questions — proposed commercial shape

Tom —

Appreciate the candor. Commercial proposal in brief:
- 90-day uplift pilot at +25% reserved capacity (monthly commit prorated)
- One-time bridge credit equal to 30% of uplift fees applied in month 1 of the pilot
- Free burst policy: two burst days during the pilot week (up to 2x baseline throughput); additional burst available at pre-agreed reduced overage rate
- SLA: p95 latency target with a defined remediation credit if missed

I'll drop a redlineable term sheet after the call; Neha will confirm the SOC2, audit logs, and retention language. If you want the longer-term price protection we can add a 9‑month cap on unit price increases for workloads covered by the pilot.

If that looks reasonable, we'll prepare the DocuSign and a short-runbook for your infra team to avoid surprises when caching is toggled.

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_term_sheet_presidio_2029.docx

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@presidio.ai>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@presidio.ai>, procurement@presidio.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Apr 2029 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal & perf questions — decision direction

Vivek / Marissa / Ben —

Thanks for the benchmark and proposal — we had an internal alignment meeting today. Summary and next steps:

- We are open to the 90-day uplift pilot. The free burst days and bridge credit are decisive for the short term.
- Engineering needs the runbook and a 48‑hour pre-enable window for prefix caching (no runtime restarts preferred).
- Procurement requests the term sheet redline by tomorrow EOD and a quick SOC2 evidence packet.
- We will not sign an extended multi-year commitment up front; this pilot is explicitly to validate the ergonomics and cost profile before considering expansion.

Can Redwood deliver the runbook and the redlineable term sheet by EOD tomorrow? If so, we can schedule a start date for the pilot in two weeks.

Regards,
Laura Chen
Head of Procurement, Presidio AI

---
